author: rabanus

lemma.la: non solum qualitatis, sed et locorum distantia
lemma.en: not only by a difference of quality, but of places

original.text: Et divisit lucem ac tenebras. Divisit namque eas, non solum qualitatis, sed et locorum distantia: lucem videlicet in superiore orbis parte diffundendo, in qua humana erat conversatio futura; inferiora vero ejus priscis in tenebris remanere sinendo.

english.text: And he divided the light and the darkness. For he divided them not only by a difference of quality, but of places: namely by spreading the light over the upper part of the world, in which the human way of life was to be, and by allowing the lower parts of it to remain in their ancient darkness.

notes: Bede's two clauses reproduced without a word changed and without a name — the commonest event on the Carolingian bench and worth one card, because it is what makes the difference of quality and of place the standing Latin answer rather than one Northumbrian's opinion. Rabanus is compiling a commentary for the schools out of the fathers, and Bede is by now among the fathers.
